svg.title: End-to-end responsibility overview
svg.desc: Setup → outbound → inbound → lifecycle → route change → offboarding is a reading order; sending and receiving are independent, and later journeys are optional. Six horizontal responsibility lanes. Domain Services includes E-Invoice Service and other named services, such as Tax Service. Each activity opens its owning spec. Exact service ownership of supporting capabilities remains open.
svg.text: Setup → outbound → inbound → lifecycle → route change → offboarding is a reading order; sending and receiving are independent, and later journeys are optional.
Read left to right · Solid: main handoff · Dashed: supporting capability / conditional action · Dotted: independent download
Domain Services includes E-Invoice Service and other named services, such as Tax Service. Supporting-service ownership remains to be confirmed in the specs.
Authorise a business and check setup requirements for the selected service.
ERP owns issuance. Recipient delivery and a required public copy have separate results.
Public and private sources converge. Saved-file download does not wait for ERP processing.
Receive platform status and business events; track required reports separately.
Change future traffic while preserving permitted work and records for earlier invoices.
Leave the service safely. Export and retention are separate from closing access.

a.title: SPEC-SEI-002

a.aria-label: Request setup through Global API SPEC-SEI-013
a.title: SPEC-SEI-013

Check business identity and authority, applicable certificate/trust requirements and the selected platform connection. Record which checks passed and any limitations; this does not activate sending or receiving.
Only for the selected purpose; certificate possession does not confer authority.
The connector handles protocol and evidence, not business interpretation.

a.aria-label: Return setup result and required actions SPEC-SEI-002
a.title: Explain which setup checks passed, which failed or remain unknown, what remains to be done and who must act. This result does not activate sending or receiving.
Conditional exception. Check authoritative external state before unsafe retry.

a.aria-label: Prepare, review and issue invoice SPEC-SEI-007
a.title: The ERP owns draft review and invoice issuance. Detailed preparation and final checks remain in SPEC-SEI-007.
No central AEAT directory is assumed. Failed lookup does not establish public routing.
Reuse candidate: qualify the Spain mapper migration, DTS contract, profile and operations before use.
SPEC-SEI-005
Use a qualified recipient route. Track recipient delivery and any required public copy separately. The owning spec explains checks and recovery.
Deliver through the qualified public or private recipient route. This does not establish buyer acceptance.

a.aria-label: Public copy, only if required SPEC-SEI-007
a.title: Conditional obligation; not another recipient delivery or a universal country default.

a.aria-label: Retrieve and preserve public file SPEC-SEI-016
a.title: Preserve original, public-copy and derived-file roles; safe storage is not dependent on mapping success.
Alternative ingress with independent private-route readiness; not a consequence of public retrieval.
Independent read branch. Apply current authority and safe-file controls; download is not acceptance.
SPEC-SEI-016
SPEC-SEI-016

a.aria-label: Provide platform delivery and status facts SPEC-SEI-009
a.title: Receive public-platform status-query results or private-platform evidence through a qualified interface. Use platform notifications only where a confirmed contract supports them.

a.aria-label: Record acceptance, rejection or payment SPEC-SEI-009
a.title: Separate authorised customer/ERP decisions and payment facts from incoming platform status information. Report a fact only when the applicable rule requires it.
Execute only the qualified country and destination obligation; reconcile uncertain results independently.

a.aria-label: Update status and identify required reports SPEC-SEI-009
a.title: Preserve platform evidence and authorised acceptance/rejection/payment facts; derive independent status dimensions and identify reports under the applicable rule. The fact and supported status can be visible while a separate report is pending. Incoming already reported facts are not reported again.

a.aria-label: Show invoice status and outstanding actions SPEC-SEI-009
a.title: Show evidence-based invoice status and outstanding actions, including separate reporting progress. Delivery evidence does not establish buyer acceptance or payment.
Qualified adapters execute independently tracked reporting actions; they do not interpret buyer or payment facts.
Keep each destination result separate from the original fact and invoice status. Reconcile uncertain reports without replaying completed actions.
Optional request to change the receiving or sending route. Full service exit is covered in the separate offboarding journey.
Check destination readiness and apply an approved boundary for future traffic. Earlier invoices retain their actual route and obligations.
Preserve permitted records and access needed for earlier invoices after a route change.
SPEC-SEI-003

a.aria-label: Coordinate exit and earlier obligations SPEC-SEI-003
a.title: Check the authorised exit scope and assign each unfinished invoice obligation a permitted owner and channel before dependent access is released.

a.aria-label: Export records and apply retention SPEC-SEI-003
a.title: Provide an authorised export and apply approved retention and legal holds. Ending the service does not automatically delete invoice records.
Only perform applicable, qualified external withdrawal or deregistration actions after the relevant continuity checks. Reconcile uncertain results before declaring completion.

a.aria-label: Return exit result and access terms SPEC-SEI-003
a.title: Report completion only when the exit checks are satisfied. Explain the approved historical-access and retention arrangements; unresolved work remains visible.
